narrative.overview:
EasyTierUI is a switchboard for a private mesh: each network is a board, each peer a line with a lamp. At rest the board is quiet — neutral layers, hairlines, readable text — so when a lamp changes (a peer falls back to a relay, the core stops, a node joins) it is the only thing that moves. Color means state, or the one action that matters on the screen; it is never decoration. This is SigNoz's night-shift discipline carried to a native, cross-platform client that also runs on phones.

Two scenes share one system on every platform: someone joining their own devices wants a yes or no at a glance (comfortable density, touch-sized targets); an operator manages dozens of nodes or stands up a control plane from a desktop, a phone or the server's web dashboard (medium density, compact only in admin tables). The same pages appear whichever role or target is selected.

The app follows the system appearance; light and dark are equal themes on one layer model. Platform chrome stays the platform's; the brand lives in the cobalt accent, the status lamps and the precision of the machine-data typography.
keyCharacteristics: Three neutral layers (floor, panel, well) with 1 pt hairlines, identical in structure in light and dark.
One chrome accent (Cobalt); green, amber and red only for link state and errors, always with words.
System UI font for people, system monospace with tabular figures for machine data.
Two radii: 6 pt for controls, 8 pt for containers; pills only for chips, switches and lamps.
Flat at rest; one shadow recipe for popups; no glass.
Quick, quiet motion (150 ms state, 200 ms overlay) that stops under Reduce Motion.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Cobalt is the only accent the chrome uses: the primary action, focus, selection, checked state and links. Cobalt anywhere else is a bug.

rules.name: The Red Is Reserved Rule
rules.body: Fault Red means failure or destruction. No chart series, badge or illustration is red; amber is not a softer red for "important".

rules.name: The Lamp Needs Words Rule
rules.body: A state is never color alone: every lamp sits next to a label or an icon with an accessible name.

rules.name: The Token, Not Hex Rule
rules.body: Colors come from theme.json through theme(); a missing role is added to theme.json (light and dark) and DESIGN.md in the same change.

rules.name: The Machine Voice Rule
rules.body: What the core or the network produced is set in the monospace with tabular figures; what a person wrote for a person is in the UI font. Never mix the two in one text run.

rules.name: The Quiet Section Rule
rules.body: Sections are introduced by a sentence-case Label in muted-foreground: no uppercase, no letter spacing, no eyebrow above a heading.

rules.name: The Flat Resting State Rule
rules.body: A surface that stays on screen never casts a shadow; it separates by one layer step and a hairline.

rules.name: The Solid Overlay Rule
rules.body: Floating layers are solid popover fills with a hairline. No translucency or blur as decoration.

rules.name: The Two-Tier Radius Rule
rules.body: Controls are 6 pt and containers 8 pt; anything else that is not a pill is a mistake.

dos: **Do** take every color from `theme()` / token classes, and add missing roles to `theme.json` in light and dark.
**Do** build on the floor / panel / well layers with 1 pt hairlines.
**Do** set machine data in the monospace with tabular figures, and people's text in the system UI font.
**Do** pair every lamp and status color with a word or a named icon.
**Do** use 6 pt radii for controls and 8 pt for containers, and the 4-point spacing steps.
**Do** keep touch targets at least 44 × 44 pt and let frames grow with text.
**Do** keep state transitions at 150 ms and overlays at 200 ms, and honor `reduce_motion()`.
**Do** keep iOS and Android headers, back gestures and alerts native.
donts: **Don't** write hex, `rgb()`, `hsl()` or Tailwind palette colors in UI code.
**Don't** use Cobalt for decoration, or a second accent in the chrome.
**Don't** use red for anything but failure and destruction, or amber as "important".
**Don't** put shadows on cards, lists, the sidebar or headers, or use glass and blur.
**Don't** use uppercase or letter-spaced labels, or an eyebrow above a heading.
**Don't** use a radius other than 6 pt, 8 pt or a pill.
**Don't** fix the height of anything that holds text.
**Don't** show a peer or network as connected before the core reports it.
